questions.q: What is a 'database' in the AWS Glue Data Catalog?
options: A logical namespace that groups related tables together and holds no data itself
A physical copy of all the data referenced by its tables
A synonym for an S3 bucket
A crawler's output log
questions.explain: A Glue database is purely a logical grouping mechanism for tables — it stores no data of its own.

questions.q: If you delete a table definition from the Glue Data Catalog, what happens to the underlying S3 data?
options: Nothing — the table was only metadata describing data stored elsewhere, so deleting it does not delete the S3 objects
The S3 objects are automatically deleted along with the table
The S3 bucket itself is deleted
The data moves to AWS Glacier automatically
questions.explain: A Glue table is metadata only; its schema, location, and partition info point at data that lives separately, almost always in S3. Deleting the table doesn't touch the data.

questions.q: What does an AWS Glue crawler actually do?
options: Connects to a data source, infers schema from the files it finds, and writes or updates table definitions in the Data Catalog
Grants IAM permissions to users automatically
Physically copies all source data into the Glue service
Deletes old table versions automatically after 90 days
questions.explain: A crawler is the mechanism that populates and updates the catalog by inferring schema from an actual data source — the AWS counterpart to a Purview scan.

questions.q: In the lesson's example, what changed between Version 3 and Version 7 of the same table?
options: Two columns gained 'Sensitive Data Element' comments flagging EMAIL and USA_SSN, from an automated classification job
The table was renamed
The S3 location changed to a different bucket
The number of columns doubled
questions.explain: The schema structure stayed the same (still 4 string columns), but comments were added identifying two columns as containing sensitive data — a common pattern after an automated PII detection pass.

questions.q: Besides AWS Glue itself, which other AWS services commonly query against the Glue Data Catalog?
options: Amazon Athena, Amazon Redshift Spectrum, and EMR
Only Amazon Glue Studio, nothing else
AWS Lambda exclusively
Amazon Route 53 and CloudFront
questions.explain: The Glue Data Catalog is a shared, central metadata store — Athena, Redshift Spectrum, and EMR all read table definitions from it.
